ideas.risks: Could stall if KMV08/Feldman/potential-based papers already give weaker assumptions that still fail exact conversion; extracting exact constants may show incompatibility rather than opportunity.
ideas.summary: Do a strict crosswalk from the atlas oracle (distribution-free, binary output, fixed excess `β`) to each candidate boosting theorem (KMV08, Feldman, potential-based): state theorem numbers, required weak condition, whether confidence/weights are returned, and whether final excess remains `OPT+α+ε` or can hit `OPT+ε`. End with a binary yes/no compatibility matrix.
ideas.title: Oracle-semantics compatibility audit for existing boosters
ideas.why_promising: This can quickly convert the current uncertainty into a definitive blocker/proxy theorem and may either certify a near-complete positive route or force a precise negative frontier.

ideas.risks: May require information-theoretic assumptions beyond current tools; finite-sample coupling under adaptive reweighting could be too complex and yield only asymptotic or high-order terms.
ideas.summary: Formalize and estimate the per-round gap parameter `γ_t` from data for the residual/clipping wrapper: define an observable statistic that lower-bounds `1/2-OPT_C(D_t)` with explicit confidence under adaptive sampling, then prove it is stable under stopping-time rounds and union-bounded over `T=poly(1/ε)`.
ideas.title: Adaptive, high-confidence estimation of round learnability gap
ideas.why_promising: The current blocker is explicitly computational: a conditional proof exists only with trackable `γ_t`; making this certifiable could complete Route A and is a testable, bounded technical subtask.

ideas.risks: Construction might depend on pathological classes and may not generalize to all wrapper families; proving lower/upper bounds may be hard and could be refuted by existing literature.
ideas.summary: Construct a fully quantified counterexample `C,D,F_t` showing an adaptive residual filter can drive `OPT_C(D_t)` to `1/2` while `OPT_C(D)` remains small, or force super-polynomial acceptance-mass decay in the same wrapper family used so far. Include quantifier order and dependence on `n,β,ε`.
ideas.title: Quantified negative witness for clipping-filter gap inflation
ideas.why_promising: A single explicit `(C,D,F)` witness would settle the route's generality and redirect effort to conditional theorems or alternate wrappers with minimal ambiguity.

ideas.risks: Could become too model-dependent; may require additional assumptions (noise/tail bounds) that weaken the generality of the final claim.
ideas.summary: Prove the implication under explicit stability assumptions: e.g., Tsybakov/Massart noise, distributional margin conditions, or bounded residual-variance with class-dependent compression. Show these assumptions imply `OPT_C` remains bounded away from 1/2 after specified reweighting and give polynomial `γ_t` lower bounds.
ideas.title: Conditional positive theorem under noise/margin regularity
ideas.why_promising: Converting an open edge into a rigorously scoped theorem is valuable progress even if unconditional status stays open, and may identify the exact additional structure needed.

ideas.risks: Need formal SQ lower-bound statements with matching query oracle; may not exist at required level of precision or may only yield weaker, non-competitive bounds.
ideas.summary: Model the fixed-slack improper oracle as an SQ query primitive with tolerance tied to `1/2-β`, then prove a conditional lower bound: no polynomial number of precision-`τ` queries can guarantee `ε`-optimal error for all classes/distributions without either stronger oracle outputs or additional assumptions.
ideas.title: SQ/precision obstruction for fixed-slack amplification
ideas.why_promising: If successful this gives the strongest principled negative evidence and explains why existing boosters incur additive floors under the current interface.

ideas.risks: Negative result may be sensitive to wrapper specifics; proving impossibility can be very hard, and a positive result may instead show only one filter tweak is needed.
ideas.summary: Search for an alternative wrapper that preserves weak usefulness without clipping by directly optimizing a bounded objective (e.g., entropic/median penalties) so that acceptance mass and margin-gap invariants are explicit by construction. Analyze whether this avoids oracle mismatch and gives polynomial inverse-polynomial mass in each round.
ideas.title: Design wrapper family with built-in gap-preserving geometry
ideas.why_promising: If clipping itself is the culprit, a principled alternative wrapper could close the gap while keeping the same fixed-slack oracle and distribution-free setting.
